comparison: Perfect alignment on abortion prevalence data from household questionnaires (C51-C56, C109, C163). Both evaluations support these descriptive epidemiological findings as internally consistent and directly reported from farmers.

Perfect alignment on seasonal patterns (C85-C87, C111, C184). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to discrepancy between visual pattern and non-significant statistical test, while peer reviewers explicitly support the finding, stating 'abortion incidence is higher during the dry season' and accepting both the pattern and lack of statistical significance.

Perfect alignment on zoonotic exposure risk findings (C98-C101, C174-C176). Both evaluations support the data on human exposure (79.2% handling products, 23.5% pregnant women exposed) and public health implications.

Strong alignment on main study conclusions (C12-C13, C102-C106, C112-C114, C177-C180). Both evaluations strongly support the feasibility demonstration and practical utility of the surveillance system. Peer reviewers also include C115-C117 (novel pathogen detection and RVF outbreak) which OpenEval addresses separately in R17-R18.

Strong alignment on stress and illness findings (C79-C82, C153-C155). Both evaluations support the finding of no association between stress and attribution, with appropriate acknowledgment of difficulty establishing causation when exposure is common.

Strong alignment on LFO performance variation (C57-C59, C108, C125-C128). Both evaluations support the descriptive statistics and lack of correlation with distance. OpenEval explicitly addresses the inference about engagement/motivation (C128) as reasonable though not directly measured; peer reviewers implicitly accept this interpretation.

Strong alignment on breed-specific abortion patterns (C67-C71, C110, C164-C166). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to potential reporting bias, while peer reviewers explicitly support the finding as 'convincing.' Both acknowledge the statistical significance, but OpenEval emphasizes the need for additional data to resolve reporting bias concerns.

Strong alignment on study design and location descriptors (C7, C45-C47, C188-C191). Both evaluations support these basic operational metrics. Peer reviewers also include C192-C194 (additional methodological details) not separately evaluated by OpenEval.

Strong alignment on abortion history data (C72-C78). Both evaluations support these questionnaire findings as internally consistent. Peer reviewers also include C171 (recommendation about herd management) which OpenEval addresses separately in R25 as UNCERTAIN.

Alignment on low sensitivity findings (C48-C50, C119-C120). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to uncertain denominators and potentially inappropriate comparison to French systems. Peer reviewers support the finding while emphasizing feasibility demonstration, treating low sensitivity as honest assessment rather than fundamental flaw. Peer reviewers also include C122-C124 (caveats) which OpenEval addresses separately in R21.

Both address attribution rate and diagnostic methods (C8, C88-C91, C148). OpenEval supports as straightforward calculation (42/215 = 19.5%). Peer reviewers affirm within broader context including delays impact (C9, C92-C94) and other findings, stating 'Aetiological attribution, achieved for 19.5% of cases through PCR-based diagnostics.'

Both address vaginal swab findings (C11, C65, C141-C145). OpenEval supports based on high collection rate and Figure 5 data. Peer reviewers affirm, stating 'vaginal swabs from aborting dams provided a practical and sensitive source of diagnostic material.' Peer reviewers also include C62-C64, C66 (additional sample collection details) not in this OpenEval result.

Both address delay impact on attribution (C9, C92-C93). OpenEval supports based on regression analysis (Table 2, p<0.001) showing substantial and biologically plausible effect. Peer reviewers affirm within broader context, stating attribution 'was significantly affected by delays in field investigation.'

Both address sex association finding and its interpretation (C94, C156-C158). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting statistically significant result but speculative explanations without supporting data. Peer reviewers support the limitations and interpretations (C150-C151, C156-C159) without challenge, accepting authors' acknowledgment of scope limitations.

Both address attribution rate comparisons and potential improvements (C149-C151). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to potentially inappropriate comparisons across different settings and speculative improvement claims. Peer reviewers accept these limitations without challenge as part of authors' honest assessment.

Both address study limitations and caveats (C121-C124). OpenEval supports these as appropriate context for interpreting results. Peer reviewers include these claims within broader acceptance of low sensitivity findings, treating caveats as part of balanced assessment.

Both address novel pathogen detection (C44, C115-C116). OpenEval supports based on primary diagnostic data and citation to Thomas et al., 2022. Peer reviewers affirm within broader context of surveillance utility, noting 'the zoonotic pathogens encountered are stated in the manuscript.'

Both address RVF outbreak detection (C117-C118). OpenEval supports based on citations to de Glanville et al., 2022 and Madut et al., 2024. Peer reviewers affirm within broader endorsement of surveillance system's practical utility for 'identifying emerging diseases.'

Both address non-significant effects of certain variables (C95-C97). OpenEval supports the regression findings as somewhat counterintuitive but potentially explained by vaginal swab effectiveness. Peer reviewers implicitly accept within broader affirmation of methodology and findings.

Both address comparison to Thomas et al., 2022 diagnostic methods (C10, C135-C136). OpenEval supports based on citation and biological plausibility. Peer reviewers implicitly accept within broader affirmation of diagnostic approaches.

Both address delay distribution and lack of distance correlation (C60-C61). OpenEval supports based on Pearson correlation analysis and Figure 2. Peer reviewers accept within broader affirmation of reporting system feasibility.

Both address herd management recommendations (C171-C173). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting recommendations lack supporting data on effectiveness or feasibility. Peer reviewers accept without challenge as part of comprehensive analysis.

OpenEval supports recommendations about LFO training and support (C130-C133) based on documented performance variation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific recommendations.

OpenEval supports recommendations about reducing delays (C137-C140) based on documented impact on attribution. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific operational recommendations.
OpenEval supports economic impact context (C160-C162) based on citation to Semango et al., 2024. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing economic significance.

OpenEval supports future research recommendations (C181-C183, C185-C187) as appropriate extensions addressing identified gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific research recommendations.
